title: How we know the miracles happened: writers known; either deceived or deceiving
pass_a_gloss: But you-will-say, those miracles done indeed are-said, but who to-know are-we-able them really done to-have-been: For not less uncertain it-seems, whether true are those miracles, than this, whether divine is that Scripture in whose confirmation done to-have-been they-are-said. I-answer. That those-things really happened, from our scriptures-themselves efficaciously to-be-proved to-be-able. For our writers those-things in-that manner wrote, that to-happen not is-able them in-this matter to-have-lied. The-one-denying indeed, or doubting true to-be what they-narrate about those miracles our writers, Moses and Paul, for-example, I-will-ask whether he-wills into doubt to-call Moses a-certain to-have-been who to-the-Israelite people laws gave, and certain volumes wrote: And likewise to-have-been a-certain Paul, who Christian doctrine preached, and wrote certain epistles which to-him are-ascribed. About this matter certainly no-one hitherto doubted, nor the-Atheists-themselves this to-deny willed, or dared. And really that is-witnessed by-fame so constant, so perennial, so by-all, even adversaries, by-consent received, that about this to-doubt, to-rave plainly would-be. Frequent indeed of-Moses and of-his writings mention is-made among the-Gentiles. Nor Jews and Muhammadans of-the-Christian religion enemies most-hostile, our Apostles to-have-been and to-have-written deny, or doubt. Which if someone that would-wish stubbornly into doubt to-call, thereto to-be-driven he-would-be, that of-his doubt a-cause he-bring, and some reason why faith he-does-not-have to-the-concordant of-the-whole-world testimony. And why he-believes rather Pliny, and Titus Livius to-have-been and to-have-written, than Moses and Paul. And certainly in-vain in this proving we-labor, since the-thing is in confession. For not those, who God's word reject, deny those authors, whom as sacred we-hold, to-have-been or to-have-written, but them true-things not to-have-written they-blaspheme. Come then let-us-see whether to-happen is-able, that true not be those-things which about those miracles by Moses and Paul are-narrated. Certainly, if true they-are-not, either deceived were they in writing, thinking to-have-happened those-things, which really not had-happened: or they-wrote with-mind of-deceiving, and tried false-things for true to-thrust. The-former to-be-said not is-able. For not those-things as from-elsewhere received they-report, but by-themselves done or seen they-testify. It-is-necessary therefore that they-willed to-deceive Moses the-Israelites, and Paul the-Corinthians, Galatians and others. And so feel profane men who Moses and Paul accuse of-imposture. To-be-seen therefore whether they-were impostors, who tried to-persuade those to-whom they-were-writing, and into whose hands their writings they-were-handing, these and those prodigies and miracles done to-have-been, when nevertheless of-them nothing done had-been.
pass_b_english: But you will say: those miracles are indeed said to have been done, yet how can we know they really were done? For it seems no less uncertain whether those miracles are true than whether that Scripture is divine in whose confirmation they are said to have been done. I answer that those things really happened can be proved efficaciously from our scriptures themselves. For our writers wrote those things in such a manner that they cannot have lied in this matter. For the one denying or doubting that what our writers Moses and Paul narrate about those miracles is true, I will ask, for example, whether he wills to call into doubt that there was a certain Moses who gave laws to the Israelite people and wrote certain volumes; and likewise that there was a certain Paul who preached Christian doctrine and wrote certain epistles ascribed to him. About this matter certainly no one has hitherto doubted, nor have the atheists themselves willed or dared to deny it. And really that is witnessed by a fame so constant, so perennial, so received by the consent of all — even of adversaries — that to doubt about this would plainly be to rave. For frequent mention of Moses and of his writings is made among the Gentiles. Nor do Jews and Muhammadans, most hostile enemies of the Christian religion, deny or doubt that our Apostles were and wrote. If someone would stubbornly wish to call that into doubt, he would have to be driven to bring a cause of his doubt, and some reason why he does not give faith to the concordant testimony of the whole world — and why he believes rather that Pliny and Titus Livius were and wrote than Moses and Paul. And certainly we labor in vain in proving this, since the matter is in confession. For those who reject God's word do not deny that those authors whom we hold as sacred were or wrote, but blaspheme that they did not write true things. Come then, let us see whether it can be that those things narrated by Moses and Paul about those miracles are not true. Certainly, if they are not true, either those men were deceived in writing, thinking things had happened which really had not; or they wrote with a mind to deceive and tried to thrust false things for true. The former cannot be said. For they do not report those things as received from elsewhere, but testify them as done or seen by themselves. Therefore Moses must have willed to deceive the Israelites, and Paul the Corinthians, Galatians, and others. And so profane men feel who accuse Moses and Paul of imposture. It remains to see whether they were impostors who tried to persuade those to whom they were writing, and into whose hands they were handing their writings, that these and those prodigies and miracles had been done, when nevertheless nothing of them had been done.
source_text:
XVII. At inquies, miracula illa facta quidem dicuntur, sed qui scire possumus illa revera facta esse: Nec enim minus incertum videtur, an vera sint illa miracula, quam hoc, an divina sit Scriptura illa in cujus confirmationem facta esse dicuntur. Respondeo. Quod ista revera contigerint, ex ipsis scripturis nostris efficaciter probari posse. Etenim scriptores nostri ista eo modo scripserunt, ut fieri non possit eos hac in re mentitos esse. Negantem enim, sive dubitantem vera esse quae narrant de miraculis istis scriptores nostri, Moses et Paulus, verbi causa, rogabo num velit in dubium vocare Mosen quendam fuisse qui Israelitico populo leges dedit, et quaedam volumina scripsit: Et similiter fuisse quendam Paulum, qui Christianam doctrinam praedicavit, et scripsit quasdam epistolas quae ipsi ascribuntur. Hac de re certe nemo hactenus dubitavit, nec ipsi quidem Athei hoc negare voluerunt, vel ausi fuerunt. Et revera id testatur fama tam constans, tam perennis, ita omnium, etiam adversariorum, consensu recepta, ut de hoc dubitare, delirare plane esset. Crebra enim Mosis et scriptorum ejus mentio fit apud Ethnicos. Neque Judaei et Mahumetani religionis Christianae hostes infestissimi, Apostolos nostros fuisse et scripsisse negant, sive dubitant. Quod si quis illud vellet pertinaciter in dubium vocare, eo adigendus esset, ut dubitationis suae causam afferret, et rationem aliquam cur fidem non habeat concordi totius orbis testimonio. Et cur credat potius Plinium, et Titum Livium fuisse et scripsisse, quam Mosen atque Paulum. Et certe frustra in hoc probando laboramus, quandoquidem res est in confesso. Neque enim illi, qui verbum Dei rejiciunt, negant authores illos, quos pro sacris habemus, fuisse vel scripsisse, sed illos vera non scripsisse blasphemant.

XVIII. Age ergo videamus an fieri possit, ut vera non sint ea quae de miraculis istis a Mose et Paulo narrantur. Certe, si vera non sunt, aut decepti sunt illi in scribendo, existimantes contigisse ea, quae revera non contigerant: aut scripserunt animo fallendi, et conati sunt falsa pro veris obtrudere. Prius dici non potest. Non enim illa tanquam aliunde accepta referunt, sed a seipsis gesta sive visa testantur. Oportet ergo ut voluerint fallere Moses Israelitas, et Paulus Corinthios, Galatas et alios. Et sic sentiunt homines profani qui Mosen et Paulum accusant imposturae. Videndum igitur an fuerint impostores, qui conati sint suadere iis ad quos scribebant, et in quorum manus sua scripta tradebant, haec et illa prodigia et miracula facta fuisse, cum tamen illorum nihil factum fuerit.
